title: Director of Preclinical Operations
text:
**Position Summary** 
**RadioMedix is seeking a proven leader to serve as Director of Preclinical Operations, heading our R&D and preclinical team and running our in vitro biology and in vivo imaging and vivarium laboratories, in close partnership with our radiochemistry team. This person will t****ake** **radioligand therapy (RLT) and diagnostic candidates** **from discovery and lead optimization through candidate selection and** **IND-****enabling studie****s, on time and with data that stands up to regulatory review. We are looking for a forward-thinking builder with a track record of leading high-performing teams, who will** **oversee a Lab Manager responsible for day****-****to-day lab** **operations, modernize our labs with new software and systems, and set the standard for a clean, safe, well-run research environment.** 
 
**About RadioMedix** 
**RadioMedix is a Houston-based, clinical-stage radiopharmaceutical company developing targeted diagnostics and radioligand therapeutics for cancer and other serious diseases. Our work spans discovery, preclinical development, clinical studies, and manufacturing, with programs built on isotopes such as Pb-212, Ga-68, and Cu-64.** 
**Key responsibilities:**
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

* **Team leadership:**
 + Provide strategic and operational leadership across Biology and Pharmacology, overseeing both in vitro and in vivo research teams.
 + Lead, hire, develop, and expand multidisciplinary R&D and preclinical scientific teams in support of the company's growing research organization, setting clear goals, priorities, and accountability.
 + Foster a high-performing, collaborative research organization with a culture of scientific rigor, radiation safety, and ownership.
 + Mentor scientific leaders, coach managers and scientists, run performance reviews, and plan succession and career growth.
 + Balance workload across concurrent programs and make resourcing calls when priorities shift.
* **Laboratory operations:**
 + Manage and oversee the Lab Manager, who runs day-to-day operation of the cell biology and in vivo (vivarium) laboratories; set priorities, performance goals, and operating metrics, and review lab performance regularly.
 + Own lab budgets and capital purchases, and oversee the Lab Manager's management of equipment (dose calibrators, gamma counters, and preclinical SPECT/PET/CT imaging systems), maintenance and calibration, and supply inventory.
 + Plan and secure isotope supply for research, coordinating delivery schedules with study timelines.
 + Maintain compliance with the radioactive materials license, ALARA principles, and dosimetry and waste-handling programs, in partnership with the Radiation Safety Officer (RSO).
 + Oversee animal research compliance with IACUC protocols and AAALAC or OLAW standards, where applicable.
 + Ensure biosafety, chemical hygiene, and radioactive material receipt and shipping (DOT/IATA) programs are in place and followed.
 + Implement SOPs, data integrity practices, electronic lab notebooks, and inspection-ready documentation.
* **Lab standards and housekeeping:**
 + Set and enforce clear standards for lab cleanliness, organization, and housekeeping across all preclinical labs and vivarium areas.
 + Hold the Lab Manager accountable for assigning owners to each lab area, with routine walk-throughs, cleaning and contamination-survey schedules, and accountability for findings.
 + Keep labs inspection-ready at all times for radiation safety, IACUC, and partner or client audits.
* **R&D and preclinical** **program execution:**
 + Establish and execute biology and pharmacology strategies across target validation, drug discovery, and preclinical development.
 + Oversee in vitro and in vivo studies, including assay development, disease models, mechanism of action, and preclinical efficacy.
 + Drive the advancement of therapeutic programs from target validation through candidate selection and IND submission.
 + Evaluate research data, guide program strategy, and make recommendations on scientific direction and prioritization.
 + Establish research capabilities, processes, and infrastructure to support the company's expanding pipeline.
 + Run a stage-gate process with clear candidate selection criteria (binding affinity, tumor uptake and retention, normal-organ clearance, in vivo stability, and therapeutic index) and regular portfolio reviews with leadership.
 + Design and deliver preclinical packages for radioligand therapeutics and companion diagnostics: binding affinity, internalization, and efflux assays, serum and in vivo stability, biodistribution and pharmacokinetics in tumor-bearing models, SPECT/CT and PET/CT imaging, efficacy and maximum tolerated dose studies, dosimetry with extrapolation to human, and IND-enabling toxicology.
 + Translate program goals into study plans with milestones, budgets, and go/no-go criteria.
 + Integrate DMPK, toxicology, translational sciences, and other research functions to advance pipeline programs, aligning study designs, timelines, and data across disciplines.
 + Oversee DMPK and radiopharmacokinetic characterization, including biodistribution, clearance and excretion, metabolism, and in vivo stability, to inform candidate selection, dosing, and dosimetry.
 + Direct the design and oversight of IND-enabling toxicology studies, in-house or at CROs, including dose selection, assessment of radiation-related and off-target toxicities, and integration with dosimetry.
 + Lead translational science activities, including biomarker and patient-selection strategies, imaging-based target engagement, and extrapolation to a safe first-in-human dose, in partnership with clinical development.
 + Select and manage CROs and academic collaborators, including toxicology studies, scopes of work, budgets, and data quality.
 + Author and review preclinical sections of IND, IMPD, and other regulatory submissions, and support responses to FDA and other agencies.
 + Track program timelines and report progress, risks, and recommendations to leadership.
 + Partner with the radiochemistry team on radiolabeled compound supply, quality specifications, and study scheduling, and provide preclinical data that informs radiochemistry and CMC decisions.
 + Ensure studies are well designed and statistically sound and produce complete, traceable data packages and study reports suitable for regulatory submissions and publication.
* **Cross-functional and business support:**
 + Work closely with radiochemistry, CMC, manufacturing, quality, regulatory, and clinical teams to move candidates smoothly from bench to first-in-human studies.
 + Support business development and partnership activity, including technical due diligence, partner presentations, and preclinical work for collaborators and CDMO clients.
 + Contribute to grant applications, publications, and scientific conference presentations.
 + Evaluate new targets and isotopes, and partner with radiochemistry on chelator and linker selection, to strengthen the pipeline.
 + Capture inventions through invention disclosures and support patent counsel on filings that protect the pipeline.

**Qualifications**

* **Education:** PhD in Pharmacology, Biology, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, or a related discipline strongly preferred. Exceptional candidates with a Master's degree will also be considered.

* **Experience:**
 + 10+ years of biotechnology or pharmaceutical industry experience in drug discovery, biology, and/or pharmacology, including 5+ years in radiopharmaceuticals.
 + Proven track record of advancing therapeutic programs, ideally radioligand therapeutics (RLTs) or theranostic agents, through IND submission, with direct involvement in multiple INDs.
 + Experience leading the biological evaluation of targeted radioligands (peptides, small molecules, or antibody-based vectors) during discovery and lead optimization through candidate selection, in partnership with radiochemistry.
 + Experience managing CROs and outsourced preclinical studies, and contributing to IND or equivalent regulatory submissions.
 + Hands-on experience directing or integrating DMPK, toxicology, and translational sciences to support candidate selection and IND-enabling packages.
 + Familiarity with in vitro radiopharmacology, biodistribution, SPECT/PET imaging, and dosimetry studies.
* **Leadership:**
 + 5+ years leading multidisciplinary scientific teams, including managing managers.
 + Demonstrated experience overseeing both in vitro and in vivo research teams.
 + Experience building, developing, and scaling scientific teams and research capabilities.
 + Demonstrated record of past success as a leader, such as programs delivered to IND or partnership milestones, teams built and retained, or labs or functions turned around or scaled.
 + Proven track record overseeing laboratory operations and managing lab managers: budgets, equipment, staffing, housekeeping standards, safety, and compliance.
 + Experience selecting and implementing lab software or systems (for example LIMS or ELN) and leading teams through the change.
 + Strong cross-functional leadership experience, working across multiple drug discovery and development disciplines.
* **Skills:**
 + Strong understanding of drug discovery and preclinical development, including target validation, pharmacological characterization, and efficacy studies.
 + Working knowledge of radiation safety regulations (NRC or Agreement State licensing), ALARA practice, and radioactive waste management.
 + Understanding of radiopharmaceutical toxicology, radiation dosimetry, and dosimetry-based dose selection for radioligand therapeutics.
 + Forward-thinking mindset: tracks scientific, technology, and regulatory trends and turns them into practical improvements.
 + Strong communication skills, with the ability to present data clearly to scientists, executives, partners, and regulators.

 
**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with alpha emitters (for example Pb-212 or Ac-225) as well as beta emitters (for example Lu-177 or Cu-67).
* Background in both therapeutic and diagnostic (theranostic pair) development.
* Experience building or scaling a preclinical function in a growing biotech.
* Experience within a growing or privately held biotechnology company.
* Experience scaling research organizations, teams and laboratory capabilities.
* Experience across multiple therapeutic programs or drug discovery platforms.
* Exposure to CMC, GMP manufacturing, or CDMO environments, and how preclinical choices affect scale-up.
* Experience supporting business development, partner due diligence, or fee-for-service preclinical work.
* Publication record in radiopharmaceutical science and active network in the nuclear medicine community (for example SNMMI).

 
**Working Conditions and What We Offer**

* On-site role with routine work in radiation-controlled laboratories and vivarium spaces; participation in dosimetry monitoring is required.
* Occasional travel to CROs, partners, and scientific conferences (estimated 10 to 15%).
* Competitive salary, annual bonus, and [equity or long-term incentive, if applicable].
* Medical, dental, and vision coverage, 401(k), and paid time off.
* The chance to shape a growing preclinical organization and bring new radioligand therapies to patients.
